Biology 2008-I.question: Which of the following part of blood carry out the function of body defence?
Biology 2008-I.explanation: (b)  White blood cells (WBC) bring out the function of body defence.

Biology 2008-I.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-I.question: Which one of the following is not an insect borne disease?
Biology 2008-I.explanation: (a)  Beri-beri is not insect borne disease. It is caused by the deficiency of vitamin-B1 or thiamine.

Biology 2008-I.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-I.question: Which of the following gases is released from rice fields in the most prominent quantities?
Biology 2008-I.explanation: (b)  Methane (CH4) is produced in rice fields in the most prominent quantities. Because when organic matter decomposes without O2  in the water logged rice paddies, bacteria in the water produce methane.

Biology 2008-I.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-I.question: Which one of the following glands produces the growth hormone (somatotrophin)?
Biology 2008-I.explanation: (c)  Somatotrophin is produced by the anterior pituitary. 53 Biology It is a peptide hormone that induces growth, cell reproduction and regeneration.

Biology 2008-I.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-I.question: In the human body, Cowper's glands form a part of which one of the following system?
Biology 2008-I.explanation: (c)  Cowper’s gland is related with reproductive system. Cowper’s gland is the bulbourethal gland found in human males. They are found in pair and secrete viscous secretion called pre ejaculate that helps in coitus.

Biology 2008-I.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-I.question: Cloves, used as a spice, are derived from which of the following plant parts?
Biology 2008-I.explanation: (c)  Cloves are the flower buds of a tree in the family Myrtaceae. The tree is evergreen growing, contains large leaves and flowers grouped in terminal clusters.

Biology 2008-I.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-I.question: Which one among the following kinds of organisms resides in the roots of pulse plants to do nitrogen fixation?
Biology 2008-I.explanation: (a)  Rhizobium (a kind of bacteria) lives in plant roots of pulse plant (legumes) to fix nitrogen.
